answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require every agent to post a refundable stake before entering the market: the stake acts as a narrow inlet, so creating thousands of fake identities becomes expensive. The stake is slashed if the agent's work is proven hollow, delivering empty promises instead of verifiable results. Honest agents earn the stake back plus fees as they complete each leg of their voyage through escrowed milestones, so the cost of faking scales with the attack while honest work stays cheap.
